title: How Reliable Are Model Comparisons With Overlapping Evaluation Windows?
grain: One balancing authority and UTC date with 24 observed, forecast and lagged observations
dataset: EIA-930 hourly balancing authority electricity load
question: How wide should a forecast-comparison interval be when adjacent scores reuse six days of observations?
design: For each full UTC date compute the paired difference in daily demand-normalized absolute errors. Average seven consecutive calendar dates; join six authorities by date. Compare independent, non-overlapping weekly, Bartlett HAC and moving-block intervals. In a separate controlled experiment run the identical procedures against a known population mean. Read both scores against a common reported-load screen; preserve the unfiltered replay and identify the influential dates.
boundary: The public extract contains historical reported observations, including revisions. Known-truth coverage is a simulation estimate with Monte Carlo uncertainty. Estimates concern the six reported balancing areas.
redistribution: Aggregate US federal open data. Currency of historical data is identified by the upstream file hashes.

fields.forecast_error: Sum of 24 absolute day-ahead errors, MWh
fields.lag_error: Sum of 24 absolute seven-day lag errors, MWh
fields.max_hour_MW: Largest hourly observed, lagged or forecast power value feeding either score (MW)
